t: Upon the determination of the Secretary of Defense that such action is necessary in the national interest, the Secretary may, with the approval of the Office of Management and Budget, transfer up to $3,500,000,000 between the appropriations or funds made available to the Department of Defense in this title:  Provided, That the Secretary shall notify the Congress promptly of each transfer made pursuant to the authority in this section:  Provided further, That the authority provided in this section is in addition to any other transfer authority available to the Department of Defense and is subject to the same terms and conditions as the authority provided in the Department of Defense Appropriations Act, 2013.

fable.w: The tempting reading is that OMB approval and prompt notification of Congress amount to consultation before a federal decision. But the Secretary of Defense, OMB, and Congress are all inside the federal government, so this is purely intra-government coordination and reporting. No state, tribe, expert, company, or member of the public is involved, and the section creates no rulemaking, hearing, advisory body, or right to sue.
fable.s: the Secretary may, with the approval of the Office of Management and Budget, transfer up to $3,500,000,000 between the appropriations or funds made available to the Department of Defense in this title:  Provided, That the Secretary shall notify the Congress promptly of each transfer made pursuant to the authority in this section

qwen_block.w: The section requires the Secretary of Defense to notify Congress of fund transfers. Congress is part of the federal government, so this is an intra-governmental notification, not participation by outside parties. There is no consultation with states, tribes, the public, or other non-federal entities.
qwen_block.s: the Secretary shall notify the Congress promptly of each transfer made pursuant to the authority in this section

opus.w: This section lets the Secretary of Defense move money between appropriations. The only other parties involved are the Office of Management and Budget (OMB), which is a federal agency, and Congress, which is part of the federal government. Approval from OMB is coordination between federal agencies, and notifying Congress is a report within the government. No state, tribe, expert, company, or member of the public takes part in the decision.
opus.s: the Secretary may, with the approval of the Office of Management and Budget, transfer up to $3,500,000,000 between the appropriations or funds made available to the Department of Defense in this title:  Provided, That the Secretary shall notify the Congress promptly of each transfer
opus.b: I'm labelling this "No". It might look like participation because the Secretary needs OMB approval and must notify Congress. Both of those are inside the federal government, so neither crosses the federal boundary.

qwen_chat.w: The section requires the Secretary of Defense to notify Congress and obtain approval from the Office of Management and Budget. Both Congress and the OMB are considered inside the federal government. The definition explicitly excludes reports to Congress and coordination between federal agencies/officials as participation. Since no outside parties (states, public, private entities) are involved in the decision-making process described, this is not participation.
qwen_chat.s: the Secretary shall notify the Congress promptly of each transfer made pursuant to the authority in this section
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that notifying Congress constitutes "participation" because it involves an external body. However, the definition explicitly states that Congress is INSIDE the federal government, and reports to Congress are a common trap for "No". Additionally, the Office of Management and Budget (OMB) is part of the Executive Office of the President, which is also inside the federal government. Therefore, all actors involved (Secretary of Defense, OMB, Congress) are internal to the federal government.
